name: crypto
description: Compute cryptographic hashes, HMACs, password hashes, derived keys, and secure random bytes in DuckDB SQL. Hash individual values or build a checksum over ordered rows.

cta.title: Cryptographic Hashing in SQL
cta.description: Install the Crypto extension to compute hashes, HMACs, Argon2 and scrypt password hashes, and secure random bytes against any DuckDB column — including aggregate hashes for dataset checksums.

quickStart.title: Hash a string with SHA-256
quickStart.description: The hash function returns a BLOB. Convert it to hexadecimal to display or compare the digest.
quickStart.note: A plain hash does not authenticate a message. Use HMAC when verification depends on a shared secret; use a password-hashing library for passwords.

introduction.title: Compute cryptographic digests and message authentication codes
paragraphs: A cryptographic digest gives a piece of data a fingerprint. An HMAC combines a digest algorithm with a secret key so a recipient can check that a message came from someone holding that key and has not changed.

Crypto makes these operations available as SQL functions over your columns. Use it to compare file or record contents, create checksums, or generate the authentication value required by an integration. When reproducing a digest from another system, match its input bytes, encoding, and algorithm.

notice.title: DuckDB 2.0 build: some stored hashes change
notice.body: In the DuckDB 2.0 build, `keccak224`–`keccak512` compute real Keccak (Ethereum's variant) instead of SHA-3, and UUID, DECIMAL and ENUM values hash with a new canonical encoding. Digests stored by earlier builds for these inputs will differ. See [Changes in the DuckDB 2.0 release](#changes-in-the-duckdb-20-release).
